statement: FAA: temporary telecommunications outage; flights halted out of an abundance of caution

statement: Duffy: a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers
source: CBS New York and The Independent quote Duffy saying the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop 'following a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers' and that FAA technicians are investigating. [CBS New York](https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/jfk-laguardia-newark-airports-nationwide-ground-stop/) · [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/sean-duffy-full-statement-faa-ground-stop-flights-b3084845.html)

statement: Mullin: a telecommunication outage throughout FAA; no indication yet of a nefarious attack
source: CBS New York, Fox Weather and The Hill quote Mullin describing a telecommunications outage and saying there was no indication as of yet of a nefarious attack, though he would not rule it out, and that this is not another 9/11. NBC, citing officials, says early signs do not point to malicious activity and that the assessment could change. Bloomberg, citing one person familiar with the matter, reports that the FBI does not think it was a cyberattack and is looking at a software update. CISA and the FBI have issued no public statement. statement: Mullin's further comments (clarity, two areas, Microsoft 365, CISA/SMART)
source: CBS New York quotes Mullin on remaining communications and planes still landing. The Well News and GeekWire quote him saying two areas in the US were unaffected and still communicating normally; he declined to name them. GeekWire also reports he sees no Microsoft link to the ground stop. Click2Houston quotes him saying CISA at DHS is looking at whether the new AI tool is involved, which officials have not established. statement: Weather Service nationwide radar website outage
source: Debunked as a separate outage. The notice news outlets quoted was stale text on a Los Angeles office page, archived as early as December 2025; the page now returns 404. NWS said there is no radar outage, that radar.weather.gov is working, and that outdated isolated webpages caused the confusion. The NCEP operations center said at 6:01 PM ET that all radar data systems and network communications were normal.
